deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It holds drafts of personal correspondence in German Kurrent, heavily crossed out and rewritten, apart from the archival label 'Riemann 26' and a folio number (88) in another hand.

(a) Top, in faint pencil: the opening of a letter to a close friend. 'Mein verehrtester Freund. Vor allen Dingen meinen innigsten [replacing: herzlichsten] Dank für Alles, was Sie auch in diesem Winter wieder für mich gethan haben; meine Schwester wird Ihnen erzählt haben, dass ich ...' The draft breaks off there.

(b) In ink: a short note addressed 'Geehrter Herr', which went through several rewrites. Its final sense is as follows. Riemann's wife (Elise), as he had told the addressee the previous afternoon, had arranged with a Frau Malmros to visit 'the Club' this evening. Frau Malmros has since cancelled for today because a Frau Voll(?) is prevented from coming. She has instead invited Riemann's wife to a joint visit to the Club tomorrow evening at 7 o'clock. 'We will therefore come not today but tomorrow evening.' A cancelled passage explains why he writes: the addressee might have wanted to invite other ladies to the Club visit, and Riemann wanted to avoid any awkwardness. A closing line apologises, since he does not know the addressee's address, for sending the note this way (reading uncertain).

(c) Bottom left: 'Herrn' followed by a list of names. These are perhaps candidate addressees or club members, read approximately as 'Betti(?) · Mariani(?) · Dahl(?) · Hügel(?)'.

Context and dating: the next folio is a salary receipt dated Pisa, 3 July 1864. Riemann wintered in Pisa in 1863/64, where he was befriended by Enrico Betti. The letter to the 'verehrtester Freund' thanking him for help 'again this winter' is therefore plausibly addressed to Betti or a similar Pisan friend. The 'Club' is presumably a social club frequented by foreigners in Pisa. All of this is my inference, not on the page.

The previous page (Fourier partial sums, Dirichlet kernel, least-squares approximation, Taylor expansions) and the upside-down algebra on the next page are unrelated to this folio.

results.what: Draft personal letters: thanks to a friend for help during the winter, and a note about postponing a visit by Riemann's wife and Frau Malmros to a club

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely personal correspondence with no mathematics. It has minor biographical interest only: it bears on Riemann's social circle in Pisa around 1863/64, possibly including Betti.
transcription_corrections: Name list at bottom: 'Zetti' is more plausibly 'Betti' (Enrico Betti, Riemann's friend in Pisa); the other names (Mariani, Dahl, Hügel) remain uncertain.
Line 1 of the pencil draft: 'innigsten' is written above the struck 'herzlichsten'; the reading 'wieder für mich gethan haben' is uncertain.
The superscript 'mittheilte' belongs above the struck phrase 'Meine Frau hatte sich' as an alternative wording; it is not a free-standing insertion.
The interlinear 'auf' replaces struck 'verabredet' before 'heute Abend'; the final sentence reads 'zu einem Besuch des Clubs verabredet.'
The final clause of the 'Ich glaubte...' passage is very uncertain; the gist is that he notifies the addressee so that no awkwardness arises regarding inviting other ladies.
